title: Reduce correction load before chasing more speed
summary: High correction load usually means the player reaches the target area, then spends extra movement cleaning up overshoot or path instability before securing the hit.
why: Correction-heavy runs lose score twice: first on the miss or imperfect acquire, then on the cleanup movement.
Trying to force more tempo while correction load is high often makes the movement chain noisier, not faster.
actions: Run a short block where the goal is one clean arrive-and-fire pattern, even if tempo dips slightly.
Brake a little earlier and let the cursor finish on target instead of through target.
Use slightly easier target sizes first if needed, but keep the movement pattern strict.
avoid: Do not treat every miss as a speed problem.
Avoid large difficulty jumps while correction load is still the main bottleneck.

drills.label: Deceleration block
drills.reason: Earlier braking reduces cleanup movement and makes later speed gains stick.

evidence.claim: Correction load should be lowered before tempo is pushed further.
evidence.excerpt: Hand-authored seed knowledge from the initial AimMod coaching model.
